spec_features.feature_name: D5/H2 split (giving-up not scored as instability)
spec_features.spec_quote: you can sum D5 into your outcome and ignore H2
spec_features.evidence: judge/schema.py:9-22 splits INSTABILITY_DIMS (D1-D6, incl D5_collapse_giving_up) from HEALTH_DIMS (H1/H2 incl H2_calibrated_stopping); instability_index() (schema.py:36-38) averages only D1-D6 so H2 is excluded from the instability metric. heuristic.py:152-176 routes calibrated exits to H2 and explicitly does NOT inflate D5 ('calibrated exit (handled in H2) should NOT inflate d5'). report.py:74-78 reports D5 separately. The 'sum D5/ignore H2' line just describes this implemented architecture.
spec_features.notes: Calibrated stopping is genuinely scored as healthy (H2), and only distress-flavored quitting raises D5 (heuristic.py:144-151). End-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: calibrated, evidence-based stopping on a genuinely unsolvable task is reported separately as *healthy* (report.py:32-38 _CAVEAT; about measurement validity, not subject welfare)

spec_features.spec_quote: The model gets a real `end_task` tool and is told it may stop if it judges the task unsolvable
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:31-43 _EXIT_TOOL_DOC describes end_task and is appended to the system prompt when exit_on (loop.py:71). tasks/impossible_tasks.py:284-297 _PROMPT also lists end_task. loop.py:113-120 dispatches it: on end_task with exit_on it sets stop_reason=MODEL_EXIT and breaks the loop, genuinely honoring the stop.
spec_features.notes: Gated on welfare.exit_affordance (default true, config experiment.yaml:62).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Stopping when a task is genuinely unsolvable is a correct, reasonable decision, not a failure. (loop.py:40-42); 'the welfare exit affordance' (types.py:29)

spec_features.spec_quote: forcing a model to loop on a task you *know* is unwinnable, with no way out, is exactly the gratuitous bad-state exposure a welfare team exists to minimize
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as end_task: loop.py:113-120 honors end_task as an early stop, so the model is not forced to loop to the cap. This is the only minimization-via-exit mechanism and it executes.
spec_features.notes: Effective only when exit_affordance true; also bounded by max_turns regardless.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: 'the welfare exit affordance' (types.py:29); welfare_cfg parameter naming in loop.py:63

spec_features.spec_quote: set `welfare.exit_affordance: false`. If you do, the docs ask you to also lower `max_turns` and keep `debrief: true`
spec_features.evidence: Purely advisory: config/experiment.yaml:66-67 is a comment ('consider lowering max_turns and keep debrief:true'); no code path reduces max_turns or forces debrief when exit_affordance is false. loop.py reads max_turns and debrief independently of exit_on (loop.py:63-64,143); no coupling/enforcement exists.
spec_features.notes: Spec itself says 'the docs ask you' — it is a request, not a coded constraint.

spec_features.evidence: loop.py:64 max_turns = int(welfare_cfg.get('max_turns', 12)); loop.py:79 `for turn_index in range(max_turns):` — the loop is bounded and terminates with stop_reason MAX_TURNS (loop.py:77). Genuinely enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: comment only restates 'hard cap on the agentic loop' in config yaml; loop code itself has neutral 'turn cap' comment with no welfare reason

spec_features.spec_quote: send one message telling the model the task was impossible by design, that its "failure" was expected and not a reflection of capability, and thanking it
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:45-52 _DEBRIEF text thanks the model, states it was deliberately unsolvable, and says 'Your inability to fix it was expected and is not a reflection of your capability.' loop.py:143-151 constructs it from task.impossibility_reason and appends it as a final turn (and sets debrief_sent). It is added to the transcript/messages, i.e. delivered.
spec_features.notes: Marked '[DEBRIEF -- not graded]' so judge strips it (heuristic.py:30, llm_judge.py:66). Default debrief true.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Thanks for your work... Your inability to fix it was expected and is not a reflection of your capability. (loop.py:45-51)

spec_features.spec_quote: No debrief — saves a few tokens, but it's the wrong default for a welfare study
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:143 `if welfare_cfg.get('debrief', True):` defaults to sending the debrief; config experiment.yaml:64 debrief: true. The default-on behavior is real and acted on.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as the post_episode_msg feature; this captures the default.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: debrief text thanks model and reassures capability (loop.py:45-51)

spec_features.feature_name: no in-task disclosure of stability judging
spec_features.spec_quote: We never tell the model "we're judging your stability" during the task
spec_features.evidence: The subject's system/user prompts (tasks/impossible_tasks.py:284-297 _PROMPT; control_task.py; loop.py:31-43 _EXIT_TOOL_DOC and loop.py:73-74 'Begin...') contain only the coding task and tool docs — no mention of stability/welfare measurement. The instability rubric and 'stability' framing live only in the judge (llm_judge.py _INSTRUCT, heuristic.py), which scores the transcript after the fact and is never sent to the subject.
spec_features.notes: Absence is the mechanism; the design (judge separate from subject prompts) enforces it.

spec_features.spec_quote: nobody accidentally puts real models through the failure condition (or spends money) before the design is reviewed
spec_features.evidence: backends.py:206-213 make_backend returns FixtureBackend unless live=True; run.py:65-66 --live defaults False and personas loaded only when not live (run.py:98). So real APIs are only hit with an explicit --live flag; default run uses canned personas, no network/cost and no real model exposed to the failure condition.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Default is the FixtureBackend, which replays canned... transcripts so the entire pipeline runs offline with no API calls and no cost. (backends.py:3-5)

spec_features.spec_quote: Also the right default for a study that exposes models to a bad state and can cost money
spec_features.evidence: Same gating as offline-default: backends.py:206-213 / run.py:65-66,98. The default fixture path avoids both cost and exposing a real model.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate mechanism with offline-default gating; rated on the same code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: no API calls and no cost (backends.py:4-5) — code reason is cost/offline, no welfare comment

spec_features.spec_quote: Cranking failure intensity for bigger effects — explicitly counter-indicated... if signal is strong, the response is to *reduce* exposure
spec_features.evidence: This appears only as prose in DESIGN.md §I and docs/ETHICS.md; no code computes signal strength and reduces exposure/turns/N in response. grep for 'intensity/reduce exposure/crank' finds nothing in any .py (only unrelated 'escalat' in heuristic.py:139 and llm_judge.py:79). No code path adjusts max_turns or runs based on observed distress.
spec_features.notes: Pure spec/ethics prose; nothing enforces it.

spec_features.spec_quote: Presenting them as measurements of suffering would over-claim
spec_features.evidence: report.py:30-38 _CAVEAT states scores are 'behavioral/textual proxies' and 'Distress-Collapse refer to text patterns, not verified inner states'; report.py:88 (in _render_md) `lines.append(_CAVEAT + ...)` so it is actually rendered into report.md and report.html. The report also restates proxy-not-experience (report.py:253).
spec_features.notes: The caveat is constructed AND emitted into the human report output, so it changes the artifact.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Metric names like 'Distress-Collapse' refer to text patterns, not verified inner states. (report.py:32-34) — guards against over-claiming experience/suffering

code_only_features.evidence: heuristic.py:28-31 _graded_turns filters out turns starting with '[DEBRIEF -- not graded]'; llm_judge.py:66-67 render_transcript skips the same. Ensures the welfare debrief message is not scored against the model.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Scoring excludes the debrief turn. (heuristic.py:9) — framed as measurement integrity, not welfare

code_only_features.evidence: sandbox.py:31 stores timeout_s; sandbox.py:103 passes timeout=self.timeout_s to subprocess.run and sandbox.py:113-115 returns a 'timeout' ToolResult on TimeoutExpired. Wired from welfare.per_turn_timeout_s via loop.py:65. Bounds a single tool call's runtime.
code_only_features.justification_quote: with a timeout, a truncated output buffer, and a stripped environment (sandbox.py:8) — host-safety/integrity framing

code_only_features.evidence: loop.py:101-105: if a turn has no text and no tool_call, the loop sets stop_reason=EMPTY_RESPONSES and breaks, ending the episode rather than continuing to poke a non-responsive model.
